body:
OBSERVED 2026-09-26 on origin/main d065c8767 (a clean detached worktree): the 47 tests/unit files
that mention limiter / kobo_auth / usermanagement / handle_login_user / api.auth, run with
`pytest -n 6`, failed 28, 65 and 54 tests in three consecutive runs. The same set run serially
passed (628 passed, 19 skipped), and so did one -n 6 run.

The errors are import-state pollution, not assertions: "cannot import name 'limiter' from 'cps'
(unknown location)", "module 'cps' has no attribute 'cw_login'", "module 'cps.ub' has no
attribute 'User'", "<module 'cps'> has no attribute 'calibre_db'". Some test evidently removes
or replaces `cps` / `cps.*` in sys.modules and does not restore it, and xdist's load
distribution decides which worker inherits the damage.

CI's full-suite run is not affected in practice (Fast Tests is green), which is why this is
invisible: it only bites a developer running a focused subset in parallel, who then sees
dozens of unrelated failures.
Suspects to bisect first: tests that reload cps (test_application_factory,
test_1882_bare_metal_hardening, test_1931_spa_reverse_proxy_auth) and any fixture that pops
sys.modules entries.
title: An ad hoc tests/unit subset under xdist fails with import-state errors on main
